data.ensure-sso-auth.sh:
#!/bin/bash
set -e

CONF=/config/qBittorrent/qBittorrent.conf
mkdir -p /config/qBittorrent
touch "$CONF"

set_key() {
  key="$1"
  value="$2"
  export KEY="$key" VALUE="$value"
  if awk 'index($0, ENVIRON["KEY"] "=") == 1 { found=1; exit } END { exit !found }' "$CONF"; then
    awk 'index($0, ENVIRON["KEY"] "=") == 1 { print ENVIRON["KEY"] "=" ENVIRON["VALUE"]; next } { print }' "$CONF" > "$CONF.tmp" && mv "$CONF.tmp" "$CONF"
  elif grep -q '^\[WebUI\]' "$CONF"; then
    awk '
      /^\[/ { if (in_prefs && !inserted) { print ENVIRON["KEY"] "=" ENVIRON["VALUE"]; inserted=1 } in_prefs=0 }
      /^\[WebUI\]/ { in_prefs=1 }
      { print }
      END { if (!inserted) print ENVIRON["KEY"] "=" ENVIRON["VALUE"] }
    ' "$CONF" > "$CONF.tmp" && mv "$CONF.tmp" "$CONF"
  else
    printf '\n[WebUI]\n%s=%s\n' "$key" "$value" >> "$CONF"
  fi
}

# qBittorrent 5.3 stores these keys in [WebUI].
set_key 'AuthSubnetWhitelistEnabled' 'true'
set_key 'AuthSubnetWhitelist' "$SSO_AUTH_WHITELIST"
# Check the connecting pod against the whitelist. Trusting X-Forwarded-For
# would check the public client IP and cause a second login after Authentik.
# Keep reverse-proxy support for HTTPS headers and secure cookies.
set_key 'LocalHostAuth' 'false'
set_key 'ReverseProxySupportEnabled' 'true'
set_key 'TrustedReverseProxiesList' ''
